## The one idea

AI-built sites look AI-built because the model keeps landing on the same defaults. Anthropic's frontend-design skill for Claude Code lists those defaults by name and makes Claude plan, review and only then code. You install it with one command, and after that it turns on by itself for frontend work. The reel stands on one specific true thing: the install is `/plugin install frontend-design@claude-plugins-official` (facts.md#2), the skill activates automatically for frontend requests (facts.md#4), and its SKILL.md even lists Anthropic's own terracotta "near #D97757" on cream as an AI tell (facts.md#5). The reel must not claim that the skill guarantees a site never looks AI-made (facts.md#12), must not present the November 2025 advice (Inter, purple gradients, bold animation) as what the skill says today, and must not invent a before/after result, a client story or a personal number.

## The viewer

Who: someone who ships landing pages or client sites built with Claude Code. That could be a freelancer, a small-agency developer or a solo founder making their own page. They can code and they use Claude Code daily, but they are not trained designers.

Their problem, in their words: "Every site I build with AI ends up with the same rounded cards, soft grey shadows and all-caps labels, and clients can tell right away. I fix one thing and the next page comes out looking the same."

The moment they feel it: they send a client a preview link, or post their launch page, and it looks like every other AI-made page in the feed. Same card grid, same shadow, a little label above every heading, an arrow on the button. They know it looks generated before anyone says it.

## The promise and the payoff

Every hook promises one of three things. The judge's winner decides which one leads, and the body should cover all three in this order:

1. **The reason**: why it looks identical. Paid by naming the tells from the skill's list (rounded cards, one border-radius, the rgba(0,0,0,.1) shadow, all-caps labels, the arrow on the button), plus Anthropic's own diagnosis, "distributional convergence".
2. **The list**: the tells themselves. Paid by the beat that reads them off, including the twist that Anthropic's own #D97757 is on it.
3. **The fix**: one command. Paid by the install beat with the exact command on screen, plus the line that it turns on by itself.

Match the payoff to the hook:
- h03 "5 AI tells": the five from facts.md#7 are an accent on one word in a headline, all-caps labels, unnecessary labels above content, '01 / 02 / 03' markers on content that isn't a sequence, and a '→' on button text. Count them on screen.
- h15 "3 edits": the accented headline word, the all-caps labels and the arrow on the button.
- h07 "5 AI looks": facts.md#5 confirms the skill lists five looks but spells out only two (cream near #F4F1EA with terracotta near #D97757, and near-black with one acid-green or vermilion accent). Name those two and don't make up the other three.
- h13 "two passes": the plan pass and the review pass (facts.md#9).
- h12 "one border-radius": facts.md#6.
- h05 "Before. After.": the creator needs their own two builds of the same prompt, filmed. No official benchmark exists, so if there's no footage, don't use this hook.

The main payoff beat is the install command on screen, followed straight away by "it turns on by itself."

## Facts to use

- **facts.md#2 (step)**: in a Claude Code session, `/plugin install frontend-design@claude-plugins-official`. From the shell: `claude plugin install frontend-design@claude-plugins-official`. Show the exact strings on screen. Say "slash plugin install frontend design."
- **facts.md#3 (step, small print)**: Claude Code adds Anthropic's official marketplace automatically the first time you start an interactive session, so most people don't need a marketplace add step. This belongs in the PDF, not the voiceover.
- **facts.md#4 (mechanism)**: once installed, the skill activates automatically for frontend work. You just ask Claude to build a UI. The README's example prompt, "Build a landing page for an AI security startup", works well as a demo prompt.
- **facts.md#5 (comparison, the twist)**: the skill lists five looks that AI design clusters around, including a warm cream background "near #F4F1EA" with a terracotta accent "near #D97757", and a near-black background with one acid-green or vermilion accent. It calls #D97757 "Anthropic's own Claude-interaction accent". This is the most shareable beat: Anthropic flags its own brand color.
- **facts.md#6 (number/comparison beat)**: the SaaS-card kit is a tell: identical rounded cards, one border-radius on everything, the same soft grey shadow `rgba(0,0,0,.1)`, and gradient washes used as decoration. Put the rgba value on screen and say "the same soft grey shadow."
- **facts.md#7 (list beat)**: the skill says the commonest tells are accenting one word in a headline, all-caps labels and unnecessary labels above content. It also flags '01 / 02 / 03' markers on content that isn't a sequence, and a '→' added to button text.
- **facts.md#8 (comparison)**: fade-and-slide-up entrances on every section and hover transitions on every card "read as AI-generated". The skill asks for one orchestrated moment instead.
- **facts.md#9 (mechanism)**: Claude works in two passes. First comes a design plan: 4 to 6 named hex colors, typefaces, a layout with ASCII wireframes, and principles. Then a review revises anything generic, and only after that does it write code. It also sets a quality floor: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected.
- **facts.md#12 (honesty beat)**: the brief's own words win. SKILL.md: "the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks." If you ask for cream and terracotta, you get it.
- **facts.md#13 (the "not your fault" beat)**: Anthropic's article (November 12, 2025) says that without guidance an LLM landing page "will almost always conform to Inter fonts, purple gradients on white backgrounds, and minimal animations", and blames "distributional convergence". Use it only as the reason AI looks samey, never as the skill's current rules.
- **facts.md#14 (proof)**: the Claude marketplace page lists frontend-design as "Anthropic verified" with 1,134,112 installs. Say "as of November 2026" or "over a million installs."
- **facts.md#1 and #11 (proof, small print)**: it's an official plugin in anthropics/claude-plugins-official under plugins/frontend-design, Apache 2.0 licensed, at version 1.1.1.
- **Numbers section (proof, optional)**: SKILL.md was last updated on 2026-09-01. That is the version this reel quotes.

## Facts to avoid and pitfalls

- **Outdated advice**: the November 2025 article's guidance (avoid Inter, avoid purple gradients, use bold animation) is not the current SKILL.md. The skill was rewritten. Quote the September 2026 tells only.
- **Motion**: the marketplace page and the README still say "high-impact animations" and "scroll-triggered interactions". The current SKILL.md says to use motion sparingly and to aim for one orchestrated moment. Never say the skill adds scroll animations.
- **Old home**: the plugin is no longer in the anthropics/claude-code repo. Don't show or link that repo.
- **Where /plugin works**: `/plugin` only works in an interactive Claude Code session. In `claude -p` it replies "/plugin isn't available in this environment." The shell form is `claude plugin install ...`.
- **Fresh machine**: if no interactive session has ever run, first run `claude plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-official`. This goes in the PDF.
- **Cloud sessions**: claude.ai/code does not load plugins installed locally. Don't imply otherwise.
- **Not instant**: in a session, `/plugin install` opens a details panel and asks for a scope (user, project, local). Don't say "it installs instantly". Say "pick a scope and you're done."
- **Not a filter**: the skill is guidance. It can't promise "never looks AI" or "undetectable". The brief overrides it.
- **The other route**: installing through anthropics/skills (example-skills@anthropic-agent-skills) brings in 12 skills. If you want only this one, use frontend-design@claude-plugins-official.
- **Safety note (optional, PDF)**: plugins can run hooks and MCP servers, and the docs advise reading the details pane before you install. This plugin contains only a skill.
- **Unverified, don't claim**:
  - the exact install output ("Plugin is now active.") was never seen for this plugin
  - the token cost shown in the details pane
  - any measured before/after benchmark for the current version
  - the secondhand LinkedIn quote
- **Personal claims**: the voice profile has no proof section filled in. No invented client reactions, revenue, hours saved or site counts. First-person pain is fine as framing ("my sites all looked the same"). A specific outcome is not.
- **The five looks**: facts.md names only two of the five. Don't list the other three.

## Suggested beat sheet

Default reel, about 32 to 38 seconds, roughly 105 to 120 words at 195 wpm.

1. **Hook (pain-payoff)**, 0 to 3 s, the judge's winning line. Frame 1 is the winner's on-screen text over a generic AI-looking card grid.
2. **Stake (pain-payoff)**, facts.md#6. "If you ship client sites with Claude Code, you know the look: rounded cards, one border-radius, the same soft grey shadow." On screen: `rgba(0,0,0,.1)`.
3. **Mechanism (why)**, facts.md#13. "Anthropic calls it distributional convergence. Without guidance, every model lands on the same page."
4. **Comparison (the twist)**, facts.md#5. "Their frontend-design skill lists the looks to avoid, and one of them is Anthropic's own terracotta, D97757, on cream." On screen: a cream and #D97757 swatch with "AI TELL".
5. **Number/list**, facts.md#7 and #8. "Also on the list: one accented word in the headline, all-caps labels, 01 02 03 on things that aren't steps, an arrow on every button, fade-up on every section." Each tell gets its own card.
6. **Mechanism (how it fixes it)**, facts.md#9. "With it on, Claude plans 4 to 6 colors, type and layout, reviews the plan for anything generic, and only then codes."
7. **Step (the payoff)**, facts.md#2 and #4. "One command: slash plugin install frontend-design at claude-plugins-official. Pick a scope, and it turns on by itself for any frontend request." Full command on screen, held for at least 2 s.
8. **Proof plus honesty**, facts.md#14 and #12. "Anthropic verified, over a million installs. And if your brief asks for a look, your brief wins." Cut the second sentence if the reel runs long.
9. **The ask**, a single closing line from the two below.

## The ask

Keyword: **TELLS**. Deliverable (NEW, to create): a one-page PDF checklist of the AI design tells named in the current SKILL.md. It covers:
- the SaaS-card kit and the rgba(0,0,0,.1) shadow
- the accented headline word, all-caps labels, unnecessary labels, false '01 / 02 / 03' markers and '→' on buttons
- fade-up on every section and hover on every card
- the cream plus #D97757 and near-black plus acid-green looks

Underneath sit the exact install commands. In a session: `/plugin install frontend-design@claude-plugins-official`. In the shell: `claude plugin install frontend-design@claude-plugins-official`. For a fresh machine, add the `claude plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-official` line.

Two candidate closing lines. Each repeats a hook word so the replay loops:
- "Comment TELLS and I'll send the checklist, so your next site doesn't look identical." (repeats "identical", pairs with h01 and h14)
- "Comment TELLS for every tell on one page, plus the one command." (repeats "one", pairs with h05, h06, h09 and h12)

This is the only ask. No follow, no link in bio, no second keyword anywhere in the reel.

## On-screen material

Screenshots in 01-research/assets/:
- **01-repo.png**: the GitHub folder anthropics/claude-plugins-official/plugins/frontend-design and its README. Proof it's official, with the example prompts. Use it for beat 7 or 8.
- **02-plugin-page.png**: the Claude marketplace page with the "Anthropic verified" badge, 1,134,112 installs and the Install in Claude Code button. Use it for beat 8. Crop out the cookie banner at the bottom right.
- **03-skill-md.png**: the SKILL.md on GitHub, showing the frontmatter description and the opening design principles with the typographic tells. Use it for beats 4 and 5 so viewers see the list is real.
- **04-blog.png**: Anthropic's article "Improving frontend design through Skills", November 12, 2025, opening on Inter fonts and purple gradients. Use it only for beat 3 (the diagnosis), never as current rules. Crop out the cookie banner.
- **05-install-docs.png**: the Claude Code docs page "Install and manage plugins" with the /plugin install flow. Use it behind beat 7.

Numbers and strings that deserve a card:
- `/plugin install frontend-design@claude-plugins-official` (the main card)
- `#D97757` next to `#F4F1EA`, shown as real swatches
- `rgba(0,0,0,.1)`
- `4 to 6 colors`, then `PLAN → REVIEW → CODE`. The arrow is fine as a diagram on screen. Just don't put it on a button mockup you're calling good.
- `1,134,112 installs`, labelled "as of Nov 2026"
- `01 / 02 / 03` with a strike through it

## Words and tones

Use: tells, defaults, generic, templated, the same look, rounded cards, soft grey shadow, all-caps labels, plan, review, then code, one command, turns on by itself, Anthropic verified, your brief wins.

Avoid: "AI-proof", "undetectable", "guaranteed", "never looks AI again", "game-changer", "hack", "secret", "brand new" (it launched in November 2025 and was updated in September 2026). Also avoid any claim about the skill adding animations, and any Inter or purple-gradient rule presented as current.

Spelling and saying:
- **Claude Code**: two words, both capitalised.
- **frontend-design**: always lowercase with the hyphen on screen. Say "frontend design".
- **/plugin install**: say "slash plugin install".
- **frontend-design@claude-plugins-official**: say "frontend design at claude plugins official".
- **SKILL.md**: write it that way on screen. Say "the skill file".
- **#D97757**: say "D 9 7 7 5 7", or just "Anthropic's own terracotta" and let the screen carry the hex.
- **Anthropic**: say "an-THROP-ic".

The voice profile shows an energetic voice with a calm tone and plain, slightly casual phrasing ("but honestly I don't really care"). Keep the sentences short and spoken.

Tones that fit:
- **insider**: the #D97757 twist and the exact rgba value feel like reading the actual file, which is what makes the reel worth forwarding.
- **warning**: the viewer is shipping these tells to clients right now, and naming them lands like a heads-up.
- **calm expert**: the plan, review, code mechanism and the honest "your brief wins" caveat build trust without any hype.
